# Judith Chapter 1 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_001_page_001.jpg

---

**1:1** In-the twelfth year of-the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, who reigned over-the Assyrians in Nineveh, the-great city, in-the days of Arphaxad, who was-reigning over-the Medes in Ecbatana —

**1:2** and he-built around Ecbatana walls of-hewn-stones, three cubits in-breadth and six cubits in-length, and he-made the-height of-the wall seventy cubits and the-breadth of-it fifty cubits;

**1:3** and its towers he-placed at-the gates of-it, one-hundred cubits in-height, and in-the breadth of-them in-the foundation sixty cubits;

**1:4** and he-made its gates, raised to-the height of seventy cubits, and in-the breadth of-them forty cubits, for-the going-out of-his armies of-power and for-the marshaling of his infantry —

**1:5** in those days Nebuchadnezzar the-king made war against Arphaxad the-king in-the great plain, which is on-the borders of Ragae.

**1:6** And there-met to him all-the ones dwelling [in] the-hill-country and all-the ones dwelling beside the-Euphrates and the-Tigris and the-Hydaspes and on-the plain of Arioch king of-the Elymaeans. And many nations of-the sons of Cheloud gathered-themselves, and they-took-a-stand in-the battle.

**1:7** And Nebuchadnezzar king of-the Assyrians sent to all-the ones dwelling in Persia and to all-the ones dwelling toward-the west, to-the ones dwelling in Cilicia and Damascus and Lebanon and Anti-Lebanon, and to all-the ones dwelling by-the seacoast,

**1:8** and to-the peoples of-Carmel and of-Gilead and of-the upper Galilee and of-the great plain of Esdraelon,

**1:9** and to all-the ones in Samaria and its cities, and beyond the-Jordan unto Jerusalem and Betane and Chelous and Kadesh and the-river of Egypt, and Tahpanhes and Rameses and all-the land of Goshen

**1:10** until one-comes above Tanis and Memphis, and to all-the ones inhabiting Egypt until one-comes to-the borders of Ethiopia.

**1:11** And all-the ones inhabiting all-the land set-at-nothing the-word of Nebuchadnezzar king of-the Assyrians, and they-did-not gather-together to him for-the campaign, because they-were-not-afraid of-him; for he-was to them as a man of one, and they-sent-back his messengers empty-handed, in-disgrace.

**1:12** And Nebuchadnezzar became greatly-enraged against all this land, and he-swore by-his throne and by-his kingdom that surely he-would-take-vengeance on all-the borders of Cilicia and Damascus and Syria, to-kill with-the sword also all-the ones dwelling in-the land of Moab and the-sons of Ammon and all-[those-of] Judea and all-the ones in Egypt, until one-comes to-the borders of-the two seas.

**1:13** And he-drew-up [battle-order] with-his forces against Arphaxad the-king in-the seventeenth year, and he-prevailed in-his battle, and he-turned the-whole force of Arphaxad and all-his cavalry and all-his chariots,

**1:14** and he-became-master of his cities and he-came to Ecbatana, and he-took-possession-of the-towers and he-plundered its markets, and he-turned its glory into disgrace.

**1:15** And he-seized Arphaxad in-the mountains of Ragae, and he-struck him down with his spears, and he-utterly-destroyed him until that-day.

**1:16** And he-returned, he and all-his company, a very-great mixed-multitude of warriors; and there he-rested-at-ease, he and his force, for a hundred-and-twenty days.
